data.body:
Re-review BLOCKed with 3 findings (E4, G1G2, G6). All three are the same defect and the reviewer is right on every point: the plan cited "16,940 ms over a 10,000-ticket store" to `docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md`, and that figure is not in that file on `origin/main`. The ADR fixture there is 630 tickets and its cost tables are token counts, not wall-clock.

The error is mine and it is specific. The ADR amendment carrying that measurement is Gerrit change 3213, which has not merged. I had moved the figure off a `[rebar:...]` ticket citation precisely to avoid declaring an upstream edge to an unclosed ticket, and in doing so pointed it at file content that does not exist yet. Swapping a ticket citation for a file citation does not make unlanded material citable; the gate reads `origin/main` either way.

Fixed by removing the figure rather than re-sourcing it. It was never load-bearing: the migration argument rests on `_ensure_schema` already raising `StaleIndex` on a version mismatch and the caller discarding and rebuilding. The paragraph now says a rebuild is paid once per installation, off the query path, and states outright that no cold-cost number is recorded in the tree -- it is measured at runtime and printed by the scale test.
